analysis.theory:
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) provides resizable virtual servers, called instances, in the AWS cloud. An instance is launched from an Amazon Machine Image (AMI), which supplies the operating system, and an instance type such as t2.micro, which fixes its CPU and memory. Access is secured with a key pair, where the private key file is used for SSH login, and a security group acts as a virtual firewall that allows only the listed inbound ports, for example 22 for SSH and 80 for HTTP.

Apache HTTP Server (httpd) is a widely used open-source web server; on Amazon Linux it is installed with the dnf package manager and managed as a systemd service. Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) is object storage organised into buckets whose names are globally unique. With static website hosting enabled, S3 serves HTML, CSS and image objects directly over HTTP through a website endpoint, without any server to manage. Objects must be made publicly readable, usually through a bucket policy, before the endpoint can serve them.
analysis.conclusion: An EC2 instance running Amazon Linux 2023 was launched, secured with a security group allowing SSH and HTTP, and accessed over SSH. Apache httpd was installed, enabled and verified as running, and the custom page was served at the instance's public IP. An S3 bucket was created, the site files were uploaded and static website hosting was enabled. The bucket policy and the S3 website endpoint loading in a browser are not shown in the screenshots provided.
